newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico budget plans seen reducing corruption.
newsitem.headline: Mexico budget plans seen reducing corruption.

text.p: Mexico said on Thursday that a planned modernization to the way it monitors government spending will cut down on corruption and facilitate communication between departments.

Deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner told reporters on Wednesday that under the planned new arrangements, the finance ministry would take responsibility for the spending of government departments and monitor whether their plans were on schedule.

"Under this scheme, the management of national treasury funds will be centralised to avoid having several petty cash sources, which are difficult to control," Werner said. "As we know there have been cases when these funds have not been managed very honestly."
A government official said on Thursday that the new measures would give the government a view of whether ministries were keeping to their spending targets rather than waiting for periodic audits.
"The purpose of these changes is to make for a more agile and opportune follow up of expenditure, simplifying it and making it more transparent," he said.
"To control these funds we need to see the film, not the photographs," he added.
The government would track expenditure via computer.
"What we want is for the Treasury to have better follow-up (on spending)," he added.
Hector Chavez, Chief Economist for Mexico at Santander Investment here, said the changes would cut down on the misuse of funds.

"The focus is to reduce corruption and it is not seen as centralising," he said. "It is part of the whole project to improve the efficiency of the way the budget is executed, to reduce corruption and improve the flow of information."
One economist here said the changes were mainly operational and would not alter the way ministries apportioned their budgets.
